title: 2 John
subtitle: The Second Letter of John - Key Notes, Cross-References, and Messianic Connections (WEB)

items.value: Second John is thirteen verses on a single sheet of papyrus. Two words carry it: truth and love, and the elder will not let anyone have one without the other.
It is a short letter with a sharp edge: love walks in the commandments, and the door stays shut to those who deny that the Messiah came in the flesh.

sections.heading: How this study is put together

items.value: Each of the shortest books in the Bible is one chapter long, so each one is a complete study in a single guide, laid out the same way as every other book in this series.

values: **Key Notes** - observations worth having in hand before you read, each ending with the verses it comes from.
**Key Cross-References** - passages that stand behind or alongside the text, grouped by theme.
**Messianic Connections** - places where the text reaches back into the Hebrew Scriptures or points ahead to the Messiah. Where an entry is a pattern rather than a prediction, the note says so.
**For Further Study** - places to go deeper.
**Introduction** - the book read as a whole before you read it in parts.
**The text itself**, printed in full in the World English Bible, with footnote markers on the verses the references belong to.

items.value: Every scripture reference is a live link to the World English Bible on BibleGateway. In the app, tapping a footnote marker shows the full text of the passages cited and a line on why they connect.

sections.heading: A note on the divine names

items.value: In the notes and introductions this study uses **Yahweh** for the covenant name of God and **Yahshua** for the Messiah. The printed scripture text is never altered; the World English Bible stands exactly as the translators set it, so our own speech and the translator's work stay visibly distinct.
The writer calls himself only the elder. Early tradition identifies him as the apostle John in old age, and the language is close to John's Gospel and his first letter.

The chosen lady and her children may be a woman and her household, or a congregation addressed as a lady. The closing greeting from the children of her chosen sister suggests one assembly greeting another.

values: **Verses 4-6** - walking in truth, and love defined as walking in His commandments.
**Verses 7-11** - deceivers who deny the Messiah came in the flesh, and the door kept shut.

chapters.heading: 2 JOHN - Truth and Love, a Commandment From the Beginning, and a Door Kept Shut
chapters.title: Truth and Love, a Commandment From the Beginning, and a Door Kept Shut
keyNotes: "The elder" is all he calls himself. Early tradition says it is the apostle John, by then an old man. The language is so close to John's Gospel and first letter that most readers hear the same voice (2 John 1:1, 3 John 1:1).

"The chosen lady and her children" may be a woman and her family, or a way of addressing an assembly and its members. The closing greeting from the children of your chosen sister suggests a sister congregation (2 John 1:1, 1:13).
Truth appears five times in the first four verses. Love appears four times in the letter. John will not let you have either one without the other (2 John 1:1-6).
"For the truth's sake, which remains in us, and it will be with us forever." Truth is not only something you hold. It is something that remains in you (2 John 1:2, Psalm 117:2).

"Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us." Not a wish but a promise: will be. The same three gifts the priestly blessing asks Yahweh to give - be gracious to you, and give you peace (2 John 1:3, Numbers 6:24-26).
"The Son of the Father" - only here in the New Testament is He called by exactly that phrase. Proverbs asks what is His name, and what is His son's name? (2 John 1:3, Proverbs 30:4).
"I have found some of your children walking in truth." Some. Not all. He rejoices in the ones who are, without pretending about the others (2 John 1:4).
"Even as we have been commanded by the Father." Walking in truth is a commandment, not a mood (2 John 1:4).
"Not as though I wrote to you a new commandment, but that which we had from the beginning." Love one another is as old as Leviticus 19: love your neighbor as yourself (2 John 1:5, Leviticus 19:18).

"This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments." John defines love by obedience, just as Moses did: love Yahweh your God and keep His commandments. Love is not set against the commandments. It walks in them (2 John 1:6, Deuteronomy 11:1).
"Many deceivers have gone out into the world." Gone out - they had been inside. False teaching usually starts within (2 John 1:7, 1 John 2:19).

"Those who don't confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh." Some teachers in John's day said the Son only seemed to have a body. John says that denies the whole thing: the Word became flesh (2 John 1:7, John 1:14).
"This is the deceiver and the Antichrist." Antichrist in John's letters is not only one figure at the end. It is any spirit that denies the Messiah came in the flesh (2 John 1:7, 1 John 4:3).
"Watch yourselves, that we don't lose the things which we have accomplished." It is possible to work hard for years and let a deceiver walk off with it (2 John 1:8).
"A full reward." Boaz blessed Ruth: may a full reward be given you from Yahweh, under whose wings you have come to take refuge (2 John 1:8, Ruth 2:12).

"Whoever transgresses" - literally goes ahead, runs on beyond. Some claimed to have advanced past the simple teaching. John says going beyond the teaching of the Messiah is going beyond God (2 John 1:9).
"He who remains in the teaching, the same has both the Father and the Son." You cannot have one without the other (2 John 1:9, John 14:9).

"Don't receive him into your house, and don't welcome him." The assemblies met in homes, and traveling teachers depended on hospitality. Taking in a false teacher meant giving him a platform and a meal ticket (2 John 1:10).
This is not about refusing to speak to unbelievers or to people with questions. It is about not sponsoring someone whose mission is to deny that the Messiah came in the flesh (2 John 1:10-11).
"He who welcomes him participates in his evil deeds." Supporting a work makes you a partner in it (2 John 1:11, Psalm 1:1).
"I don't want to do so with paper and ink." Papyrus and ink were the materials. Some things are better said in person (2 John 1:12).
"To speak face to face" is literally mouth to mouth - what Yahweh said of Moses: with him I speak mouth to mouth, plainly (2 John 1:12, Numbers 12:8).
"That our joy may be made full." Joy made full is the same phrase the Lord used the night before the cross (2 John 1:12, John 15:11).

intro: Second John is a single sheet of papyrus, thirteen verses, from the elder - by early tradition the apostle John in old age - to the chosen lady and her children, perhaps a woman and her household and perhaps a congregation, since the closing greeting from the children of her chosen sister sounds like one assembly greeting another. Two words carry the letter: truth, five times in the opening lines, and love, and John refuses to separate them.

He rejoices that some of the lady's children are walking in the truth - some, not all - and reminds her of a commandment that is not new but from the beginning, as old as Leviticus 19: that they love one another. Then he defines love: this is love, that we walk according to His commandments. It is the definition Moses gave, love Yahweh your God and keep His commandments, and it sets love and obedience on the same side.

The warning follows. Deceivers have gone out - from among them - who will not confess that Yahshua the Messiah came in the flesh, and John calls this the spirit of antichrist, since the whole faith rests on the Word made flesh. His readers must watch that they do not lose what they have worked for, because whoever runs ahead of the teaching of the Messiah does not have God, and whoever remains in it has both the Father and the Son. Since the assemblies met in homes and traveling teachers lived by hospitality, they are not to take such a teacher in or welcome him, for that would make them partners in his work. John breaks off with much left unsaid, preferring to come and speak face to face, mouth to mouth as Yahweh spoke with Moses, so that their joy may be full.

verses.1: The elder, to the chosen lady and her children, whom I love in truth; and not I only, but also all those who know the truth;
verses.2: for the truth’s sake, which remains in us, and it will be with us forever:
verses.3: Grace, mercy, and peace will be with us, from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
verses.4: I rejoice greatly that I have found some of your children walking in truth, even as we have been commanded by the Father.
verses.5: Now I beg you, dear lady, not as though I wrote to you a new commandment, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.
verses.6: This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, even as you heard from the beginning, that you should walk in it.
verses.7: For many deceivers have gone out into the world, those who don’t confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the Antichrist.
verses.8: Watch yourselves, that we don’t lose the things which we have accomplished, but that we receive a full reward.
verses.9: Whoever transgresses and doesn’t remain in the teaching of Christ, doesn’t have God. He who remains in the teaching, the same has both the Father and the Son.
verses.10: If anyone comes to you, and doesn’t bring this teaching, don’t receive him into your house, and don’t welcome him,
verses.11: for he who welcomes him participates in his evil deeds.
verses.12: Having many things to write to you, I don’t want to do so with paper and ink, but I hope to come to you, and to speak face to face, that our joy may be made full.
verses.13: The children of your chosen sister greet you. Amen.

cites.text: For his loving kindness is great toward us. Yahweh’s faithfulness endures forever. Praise Yah!
All of your words are truth. Every one of your righteous ordinances endures forever.

2.why: Yahweh's faithfulness endures forever, and all your words are truth

cites.text: ‘Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’

3.why: Yahweh bless you and keep you, be gracious to you, and give you peace

cites.text: Who has ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has bound the waters in his garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if you know?
I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.

3.why: what is his name, and what is his son's name, and you are my son

cites.text: Teach me your way, Yahweh. I will walk in your truth. Make my heart undivided to fear your name.
I have no greater joy than this, to hear about my children walking in truth.

4.why: teach me your way and I will walk in your truth, and no greater joy than children walking in truth

cites.text: “‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh.
Brothers, I write no new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which you heard from the beginning.

5.why: love your neighbor as yourself, and an old commandment which you had from the beginning

cites.text: Therefore you shall love Yahweh your God, and keep his instructions, his statutes, his ordinances, and his commandments, always.

Now, Israel, what does Yahweh your God require of you, but to fear Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul, to keep Yahweh’s commandments and statutes, which I command you today for your good?

6.why: love Yahweh your God and keep his commandments always, to walk in all his ways and to love him

cites.text: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
For to us a child is born. To us a son is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

7.why: the virgin will conceive and bear a son, Immanuel, and to us a child is born, Mighty God

cites.text: If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you, and he gives you a sign or a wonder, and the sign or the wonder comes to pass, of which he spoke to you, saying, “Let us go after other gods” (which you have not known) “and let us serve them”; you shall not listen to the words of that prophet, or to that dreamer of dreams; for Yahweh your God is testing you, to know whether you love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

Beloved, don’t believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit who confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God, and every spirit who doesn’t confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God, and this is the spirit of the Antichrist, of whom you have heard that it comes. Now it is in the world already.

7.why: do not listen to the prophet who leads after other gods, and test the spirits

cites.text: May Yahweh repay your work, and a full reward be given to you from Yahweh, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”

8.why: a full reward from Yahweh, under whose wings you have come to take refuge

cites.text: Give sincere homage to the Son, lest he be angry, and you perish on the way, for his wrath will soon be kindled. Blessed are all those who take refuge in him.
“Come near to me and hear this: “From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time that it happened, I was there.” Now the Lord Yahweh has sent me, with his Spirit.

9.why: homage given to the Son, and the Lord Yahweh has sent me, with his Spirit

cites.text: Blessed is the man who doesn’t walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;
One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.

10.why: blessed is the man who doesn't walk in the counsel of the wicked, and a companion of fools suffers harm

cites.text: With him, I will speak mouth to mouth, even plainly, and not in riddles; and he shall see Yahweh’s form. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?”
Yahweh spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. He turned again into the camp, but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.

12.why: with Moses I speak mouth to mouth, and face to face as a man speaks to his friend

cites.text: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.
The Yahweh’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”

12.why: in your presence is fullness of joy, and everlasting joy on the heads of the ransomed

parts.title: Major Themes in 2 John
items: An old man who called himself only the elder
Truth and love, never one without the other
Truth that remains in us forever
Grace, mercy and peace promised, not only wished
Rejoicing in the children who are walking in truth
A commandment from the beginning: love one another
Love defined as walking in His commandments
Deceivers who went out from within
The Word who came in the flesh
Watching so we do not lose what we worked for
Running ahead of the teaching and leaving God behind
Having both the Father and the Son
A door kept shut to those who deny Him
Some things better said face to face
